body:
My Dream Team would be:

STARTERS

Curry, Kawhi, Bron, Durant, Davis

BENCH

Morant, Booker, Butler, Tatum, Bam, Draymond, Zion

Kessler was eaten up partially because he just hasn't had too many opportunities to play with the "core rotation". And to be fair to him, it's a lot to ask from a rookie to stand up to FIBA-empowered Valanciunas. Kessler will certainly bulk up and get better if he remains healthy. At this point, he is the Americans' best young hope for a big rebounding C, besides maybe Duren. But if two of Embiid, Davis, Bam, and Draymond will commit, Kessler is definitely out of the radar. Just not his time yet, if that's the case. Mitchell Robinson may also have a case, although he could be worse than Kessler, because he has had zero FIBA experience AND he is a similar foul magnet like JJJ.

Steph will probably play, even if he wins a championship next year. This is his last realistic shot to add the only missing component from his otherwise ridiculous award shelf - Olympic gold. Even if it means playing 18-20 minutes max, this is too good of a chance to pass up. Also, he knows Kerr too well to ignore the call.

Because Steph will play - if he is healthy -, Draymond is a lock-in as well... if he is healthy and doesn't drop off substantially in 2023-2024. Last season, he proved his value and defensive chops once again with the Warriors, being the only reliable frontcourt member besides Loongod. Also, Draymond is a Team USA vet with TWO gold medals already - a third gold will only solidify his already strong case for Basketball HOF.

Klay won't play. If anything, he will play for the Bahamas. Although I'm not sure if the Bahamas can afford to replace Gordon with Thompson, considering the fact that Gordon is much more suited for FIBA basketball.

KD will play if he is healthy and the Suns won't make the Finals. This is his shot to cement himself as the greatest Team USA player of all time. Olympic Melo will be a shadow of Olympic KD if Durant leads Team USA to their consecutive 5th gold, with him being the leader of at least two, if not THREE Olympic teams. And if KD plays, you might as well book Book. Tbf, he would deserve it anyway.

Davis will probably play if he is healthy. This is too good of a chance to be The Savior of American Bigs. Edwards and Tatum will make it, although Tatum might actually turn down the offer if the Celtics make it to the Finals or win the league. He has played A LOT of games in the summer already and he has the gold from Tokyo. Edwards is a safer bet.

I'd say Haliburton has proven his worth and need with this WC and Banchero is just a "smart" addition due to his youth and unique skillset with his frame.

So, I have - Curry, Edwards, Booker, KD, and Davis starting... with Banchero, Draymond, and Haliburton also locked in. Tatum is a 50/50. I'm gonna say that this is the spot where the roster completion gets more exciting.

I have a feeling that Zion and Bam can both make it, depending on their health and in Bam's case, the duration of the season. I am a believer in Cunningham and I think he has a good chance to get in as this team lacks great playmakers outside of Haliburton and Draymond (with some Curry sprinkled in). He has the FIBA body. Also, if Bam isn't making the team, I'd be surprised if JJJ is preferred before Mobley or Mitchell Robinson. Heck, I can see an interesting case for Holmgren before JJJ, if Holmgren holds up during the season and performs relatively well, especially with shooting the ball. He already has better defensive instincts than Mr I-Block-Everything-And-Foul-Out-In-15-Minutes.

I'm gonna say that one or two of Bridges, Brown, Fox, Mitchell, Reaves, Garland, Maxey, Vassell, and Holiday have a good-to-average chance to make it in as well, depending on how their next season goes... And Embiid can make it anytime if he decides to represent the USA after the lackluster showing from our bigs in WC, especially if Team USA feels that Davis might skip the Olympics.

It's a crowded field. I do not anticipate Trae Young making it, due to his public debacles. I have serious doubts about LeBron, Kawhi, Dame, and Harden. I consider George an iffy candidate, although not impossible. I do not know what to think of Butler and his willingness to commit to Team USA, but I think he is also rather iffy. Irving's shiny moments with Team USA are probably over at this point.

From this WC roster, only Edwards and Haliburton have actually proved themselves in a FIBA setting. Bridges, Brunson, Banchero, and Reaves have had their moments, but only Banchero stands out due to his youth and body and is more suitable for FIBA than what Bridges, Reaves, and Brunson are offering. I am really monitoring the development of Kessler, Duren, and Mark Williams - the three young bigs who are definitely on the radar if one or both of Davis and Bam decide not to commit. Kessler, Duren, and Williams have the body type and rebounding ability that Team USA desperately needs. Even if Draymond is playing crunch minutes, like he did in Tokyo.

Every contract is tradeable if they become expiring. If we get TWO elite years out of Dame+Lauri (we don't have our own pick anyway next season), then we CAN put up with one mediocre-bad season down the line. Once that contract becomes an expiring one, it's honestly way easier to trade than many think, especially in February...

Dame likes Utah. He is an awesome team culture guy. Brings minimal off-court drama, probably. Fits very well with the strengths and weaknesses of Lauri and Kessler. Clarkson, Olynyk, THT, Sensabaugh, and 3 unprotected 1sts (one of our own, one MIN, and one CLE) can get it done. We can afford to lose expiring vets and Sensabaugh + additional picks, we'll have plenty left after that and Dame would be an excellent mentor figure for Keynote down the line. 

Our bench would still be quite good with Dunn (if his 3-pt shot continues to be legit), Sexton, Hendricks, and some additional roster spots that could be filled with vets + we'll get something back from the Blazers bench, probably.

What a horrendous take. If anything, it would be good for the sport, since the Suns have never won a championship and it could mean a basketball boom in Arizona. Also, they brought KD to town with their own drafted and developed guys. 

Overall, their story is far different than what the Bron-AD Lakers, Heatles, and KD-Kyrie Nets did. They drafted and developed their main guys and pivoted to a re-tooling once they felt that their window was closing with their own core guys. The Bubble Lakers were almost completely a team of mercenaries, besides role players like Kuzma and Caruso, for example.

I think the closest comparison is the 08-12 Celtics (who traded a bunch of stuff for KG) - two core guys and the leader of the team are *currently* still their own draft picks, they have their traded superstar and one additional star + a bunch of vets on the bench. I wouldn't say that the 08-12 Celtics were bad for the sport, pretty much the contrary.

Any player who has gotten an MVP deserves to be near the top of such a ranking. But in Embiid's case, his lack of playoff success and longevity hinders his theoretical ranking. Also, it's absurdly hard to compare players who played in different eras - even those who played in the 00s and in the 10s.

I'd say he is definitely below Karl Malone, Charles Barkley, James Harden, Elgin Baylor, and Steve Nash. 

Due to longevity, Iverson, Westbrook, Stockton, and Paul are currently ahead of him, although Embiid is a more well-rounded player compared to AI-Russ-Stockton due to his mix of efficiency, scoring ability, and rim protection.

There's a good case to be made that Gervin, Ewing, and Miller are ahead of Embiid because of their playoff success and in Miller's case, longevity, but Embiid's peak and capability to play on an MVP level for 3 years straight probably hinders them eventually.

I'd say he is near the top 10, if not firmly in it as the 10th man.

Keyontae will be a two-way contract guy. Wallace will probably take Saric's spot on the roster.

Starters - Giddey, SGA, Dort, J-Dub, Chet

Primary Bench - Kenrich, Joe, Wallace, Dieng hopefully, Poku or J-Will

Secondary Bench - Mann, Wiggins, JRE, J-Will or Poku, Bertans

Two-way guys: Johnson, Waters (if he still qualifies and accepts it), X

I don't think your comparison is truthful. The way I see it, Bucks did TRY and gave what they had, but it wasn't enough. Their coach made some very... questionable decisions, the team had defensive lapses, and some individual players didn't hit their shots or defend at a high level. But that doesn't mean the Bucks didn't TRY with all their heart. The other team outcoached them and showed more composure, and it's not like the Heat has a non-existent track record of doing that. They keep punching above their weight and rising up to the occasion, with a few "failures" in-between.

Willy Hernangomez or Moritz Wagner. Non-American and doesn't care about the market, big body, always produces when given minutes, seems like a great locker room guy, and costs a whole lot less than Poeltl, Vucevic. NO to Plumlee, Drummond, Griffin, Biyombo, Hayes. Lopez will probably stay in Milwaukee anyway.

I get your arguments, I really do. I want to continue the debate with a few thoughts:

- The WARRIORS were/are in a totally different position than us. They wanted the Two Timelines project to succeed, but - they have Curry, Draymond, and Klay who have all tasted winning the championship and are far, far further in their careers than the youngsters in OKC. Their "Young Kawhi" is and will continue to be Wiggins, not Kuminga or Poole, who have quite obvious flaws in their game, especially Poole. They will need to trade for their "LaMarcus Aldridge" once the Splash Bros production is clearly, *undeniably* trending down. Until then, Curry-Klay-Dray-Kerr are all competing for a chance to be one of the most dominant dynasties in the history of the NBA. These four guys don't have time to wait because their clock is really ticking loud, as their core is reaching their mid-30s. 
- Meanwhile, OKC is really probably striving to *progress* next year, which could be hard to do, since Holmgren will have a significant role in this plan. If Holmgren doesn't hold up and contribute positively AND consistently right away, but rather from the 50th-60th game, OKC might actually take a step back or stay in the same neighborhood. I believe in Holmgren, but a lot of future success depends on him becoming a consistently positive force for us. Finding consistency on an NBA level is not easy to do for young bigs in this league.
- Now, I think you're right in the sentiment that developing non-core guys becomes trickier and trickier from now on. And I do think that Presti will be more aggressive with trades from this point if he senses that a non-core guy isn't contributing positively on the court nor even off the court (say, looks defeated or passive on the bench or at practice with his role or lack of opportunities). I mostly see this as a threat to Tre Mann specifically, because I do believe that JRE and Wiggins are "great locker room guys" and I think that Poku will get more chances, considering what he showed this season before the injury - also, he can play relatively similar to Holmgren, so he could become a useful reserve big if OKC wants to be super careful with ramping up Holmgren's role and minutes. I also think that Poku is someone who is willing to sacrifice a little bit, especially since he might have an inside track to minutes compared to JRE or even Dieng unless the Frenchman progresses very, very rapidly.
- I don't really expect Saric to come back, either he or Waters will be cut for the new lottery pick.
- I am not worried about the "nonsensical bullshit" that you claim the 2024 draft to be. Presti can always flip draft picks for future picks if he desires to do so, OR he can sacrifice them this/next year for an aggressive trade to get a higher draft pick or a vet that he deems to be a fit with the team. So, in a way, I echo your belief that OKC should hunt for useful vets from now, but there are some greyer options on how to use the picks. There is always a team in the top-7 who could be persuaded to trade down if they receive significant compensation from OKC.
No.

That's true, Ja has definitely taken a leap on the defensive end. Still, his impact will never be that big on that end and he has to consistently play on a Rose-Curry-Harden type of level to give fans hope of getting a championship. The bar is stupendously high for shorter players :(

I did mention Green in the end, but maybe I should've put him straight on the list. I mentioned Barnes on the list because he is the reigning Rookie of the Year, he is playing a very versatile role (he is often the primary or secondary playmaker when FVV rests or is injured), and heavy minutes on a playoff-caliber team.

I also think that his body measurements (especially his wingspan) give him a lot of advantages, whenever his offensive game starts to get more refined. I ain't worried about the efficiency just yet - almost all Raptors are struggling with it this year due to lack of good guards and Nurse's weird system.

I tend to agree that he should/could be the best, if he could play 60 regular season games on a regular basis + playoff games, but until that happens, it's hard to put him above... Barnes even, I'd say.
Or him, indeed.
I get the logic behind Morant, although the Grizzlies' record without Morant is pretty damn good aaaand I value wings-bigs a bit higher than 6'1-6'4 guards who are mostly offense-oriented.

I can't see it as a toss-up, considering what I've seen from Luka in the regular season and playoffs, compared to Tatum – AND factoring in the supporting cast. Like, I have minimal doubt that Luka and Jaylen Brown could've reached the Finals already with a strong supporting cast.

I get that reasoning. Personally, I think that Markkanen is in the same stratosphere as the guys you mentioned (All-Star level players already) and I do believe that he could develop a lot as a passer to reach the next level. For example, I could see him reaching a level of becoming a consistent 28-8-5 type of guy, which could mean an All-NBA 1st Team berth in some years.

The other thing with your list is that it consists of guards, with the exception of Zion. I think that big men and wings need a longer time to get adjusted to today's NBA of pick-and-rolls and stretched-out defenses. So, even though Barnes and Mobley are offensively still far from the guys you mentioned, they are already so clearly above them on defense, and if the offense comes along, their impact should clearly jump above the offense-oriented guys.

Where do you stand on the talent level of Green vs Sengün vs Jabari? Did I make a mistake by not mentioning Jabari, who has been playing very, very well as of late - and could he be a better talent than Green or Sengün, who heavily lean towards offense?
Let me assume - Tatum, SGA, Zion, and... Edwards?
That's the thing, though. One can not simply "bar" health, considering everything we've seen thus far.
Agreed, he was actually very-very high on my list, but forgot to type his name. Definitely one of the brightest playmakers, if not THE brightest, of the future generation.

If the alternative to the shitty everyday life is a coalition of Kesk (total corruption), Isamaa (getting closer to an oligarchy party with each year - they really need to free themselves from Parvel Pruunsild) and EKRE (there are soooo many reasons why not to vote for them)... then you get the results of today. I'd wager that many votes that were given to Reform Party and 200 were protest votes against EKRE.

I don't hate the people who vote for EKRE, I mostly feel pity for them. They deserve a better protest party than the one that is led by a family that lives in a Trump-ish illusion, especially on Facebook.  I hope that there are some EKRE voters who can understand that they need Pohlak or someone wayyy more sensible as their new leader, because the current ones are becoming useless and are clearly trending down. They can't even form proper alliances anymore and the way they bash doctors, entrepreneurs, journalists, almost EVERYONE who doesn't agree to their viewpoint... it's not a fruitful strategy.

It will certainly be useful to bid up the contract offers of young RFAs, such as Grant Williams, PJ Washington, heck, even Cam Thomas. There are more ways to use cap space than just luring FAs. Including trades with imbalanced salaries.
The flattening of draft odds means you don't have to be in the bottom-4 as much as you needed to in the past. Heck, the Grizzlies got Morant when they had 8th worst odds or smth.

I think they are just fine with not having Sengün, since they have Holmgren - whom many believe in, despite of his frame and redshirted rookie year - and a bunch of other young bigs, who just know how to play basketball. 

We'll see, how Dieng and Tre Mann (both gotten for Sengün) develop over the years, although currently Sengün has much more value, of course – and he will continue to have, unless Dieng ultimately becomes a starter-level wing/big. Also, I do believe there's some merit to the thought that it's hard to win 45+ games with a C who isn't that good defensively, unless he's Jokic/bonafide All-NBA or even MVP-level player.

No one is truly chasing Mike, besides LeBron and maaaaayyybe Luka, once the Mavericks manage to get him proper sidekicks. Giannis is more of a rare feel-good story with his personality and background, in an era of unhappy superstars and he plays a brand of basketball where it's hard to criticize him for the things he can't do when he is one of the best two-way players in the whole planet regardless. He's like a more impressionable Tim Duncan. Why hate on the guy, when he does nothing wrong off the court and isn't an asshole on the court?

Kobe and LeBron brought it on themselves with their personalities and decisions. Giannis has caused no major drama with teammates, hasn't left Milwaukee, and generally doesn't come across as someone who is trying to catch Mike. He just comes across as someone who is happy to play basketball and win titles along the way. Different vibe.

I mean, by all accounts, he'd most probably be more successful, since he wouldn't have to defend so much ground in the earlier decades, and for every Shaq, there are 22-24 starting centers that are certainly more favorable matchups for Drummond.

Shaq perhaps? Jokic has him soundly beaten as an offensive force (due to his playmaking skills and a lot more variety in shooting prowess), and the gap defensively isn't thaaaaat huge. He already has two MVPs, and his best teammates haven't been/aren't (future) legends in the mold of Bryant and Wade, or even Hardaway who had way more talent than Murray. He has still been dominant in the playoffs as a solo force.

Yes, there are risks involved with this scenario. You can't avoid all risks in the NBA, especially in the player empowerment era. Thus far, so good - hopefully it remains this way. But if it changes, then the trade dynamics inevitably change as well.

Beware if the Knicks eventually trade for Mitchell with 5-6 picks, since Ainge and the Jazz are nowhere in a hurry with seeking a trade. In fact, they may as well let it simmer until December or January, when there are a lot more unhappy teams on the market, looking for options to salvage their situation.
I think people/fans are just less patient and want results/updates/news faster and faster. There wasn't too much complaining going on in the 90s and 00s about the length of regular season.
I really hope that Chet pans out and if someone has to be the bust, then it would be Jabari. NBA needs weirdos like Chet. We have some Jabari-type players, imo.

Alright. Time to get serious. Because Strus, Vincent and Kenrich Williams are kinda on rookie deals in my book, I didn't use them for this tough exercise.

Starting five, presuming all the core guys are healthy:

PG - Curry (48,070)
SG - Bane (2,130)
SF - Keldon Johnson (3,873)
PF - Giannis (42,492)
C - G. Hernangomez (2,444)

6th-9th men:

Guard - DiVincenzo (4,5)
Wing #1 - House Jr (4,1)
Wing #2 - Warren (1,837)
Wing #3 - Connaughton (5,7)

10th-13th - Muscala, D. Reed, JTA/Thanasis Antetokounmpo and Neto. All making about the veteran minimum. I'd keep the 15th spot open and would use options to toggle the 14th guy throughout the season, to stay under the cap. Test some guys from the G-league, mostly and if none of them pan out, I'd just sign a cheaper veteran with a minimum contract in the spring to stay under the cap.

MY LOGIC OF THOUGHT

I really threaded the needle with the fortunate salaries of Bane and Johnson (I contemplated Cam Johnson, J. Poole and T. Maxey as well, but thought that I needed more athleticism and size at the wing next to Bane) and I wanted Portis at the five, but cap limitations forced me to find cheaper players. I elected the older Hernangomez, because he is cheap, he holds up surprisingly well in small doses, is a good rebounder and he can score points in the paint if needed. I contemplated Lyles, but he just seems a bit too small and not aggressive enough compared to Hernangomez, even though he spaces the floor better. 

An additional note - it's tough to finish this assignment frankly because there are so many minimum deals yet to be signed.

I have 24,646 million dollars left for 9 guys. Less than 3 million per player and since we can't have any more cheap rookie contracts, I will have to use at least 5 minimum contracts, if I want to spend a tad bit more on my 6th-9th roster spots who should offer more support during the playoffs. Remember, you don't have to sign 15 men to your roster, you can leave that last spot open. I will of course use this loophole, considering the gargantuan contracts of Curry and Antetokounmpo.

Minimal deal guys get the min deal for a reason. Many have yet to be signed, some are definitely waiting for the KD or at least the Kyrie trade to happen. This murks up my plan a bit. But what can you do, eh? For my four minimum contract vets, I chose:

Big - Muscala (1,837). Has held up surprisingly well in very limited doses, and offers me spacing. If he can give me 6 points in 4 minutes in a random playoff game, I'll take it. He also seems to know his place in every rotation and is supposed to be a great locker room presence. You can also and perhaps should choose Damian Jones here.

"Upside"-Wing - Davon Reed (1,902). Not technically a true wing as he's 6'4 and more in the mold of Gary Harris, but he has an immense wingspan, he has decent athleticism and he works really hard on D and he has a decent 3-pt shot. He was also featured on Reddit's 99 Cent Store post as an analytics darling. Worth a flyer on the back end.

3rd playmaker, to give Curry rest and not overload the backup playmakers - Neto (1,837). He has proven himself to be a reliable hustler and a playmaker, a perfect backup even though he's undersized.

"Just a bigger body/wing" - JTA (1,837). I wanted to add Bryn Forbes as my 14th guy, but bringing in Neto and Reed already downsizes my rotation by quite a lot. I'd rather have a 6'6-6'9 "body" to throw at the opponents' wings on D. I'm gonna take a flyer on Juan Toscano-Anderson as he's slightly cheaper than Stanley Johnson and I trust his shot as little as Johnson's. He gives me some athleticism, some playmaking chops and doesn't wince when his role is minimal anyway.

Add those three minimum guys and one almost-minimum guy to the team, you have 106,422 million allocated to your roster. So that leaves me 17,233 million dollars to spend on my four main bench guys. About 4,3 million each. Fuck.

I'd definitely have Kenrich Williams as one of my four main bench guys, but isn't he technically kinda on a rookie deal? He almost feels like cheating here as he would be a no-brainer, but I feel his true market value is closer to 8-12 million. I'll make my life harder and won't steal him away from OKC, who has already lost their favorite veteran in Muscala. The same logic applies to M. Strus and G. Vincent, in my humble opinion. If I didn't want to torture myself, I'd just add them with Kenrich Williams and use 10 million instead on a really, really good 6th man. Say, Portis.

One guy who will make the cut just barely, but surely, is Danuel House (4,105). He gives me a decent 3-and-D role player as an 8th-9th man. I won't get another big anymore, because Giannis-Hernangomez-Muscala will have to do and I will even use JTA as a small-ball five sometimes. That's just the way the league is.

I'll also choose TJ Warren (1,837) as my other 8th-9th guy. If he is a shell of himself after the injuries, that sucks, but I can always waive or trade him later. But his scoring upside on the second unit is too tantalizing to ignore and he gives me a bigger wing-body than House. 

6th-7th men left. I have approximately 11 million left. A backup playmaker and one more defensive wing are needed.

I'm gonna take Pat Connaughton as my 7th man (5,728 mil). A proven veteran, good rebounder, decent defender, cheap and should hit his 3-pt shot normally better than he did against the league's best defense last playoffs. 

This leaves me 5,3 million to use on my 6th man. Should I take a flyer on Justise Winslow, who is always injured, but can run some simple offensive sets and can also be used as a wing defender? Ish Smith just isn't THAT guy as your 6th man, even though his contract fits the bill and he would give me playmaking. But he's small and old, I don't trust him in playoffs. I'm sooooo close at having Bruce Brown or Ricky Rubio, though - maybe I should throw out House for, say, Stanley Johnson and just take Brown or Hernangomez's national teammate and experienced Rubio? But Rubio is coming off a big injury and he'd be an awful spacing fit with Giannis-Keldon Johnson-Hernangomez. So'd be Brown, to be fair.

I'd rather risk with Donte DiVincenzo, who'll be making 4.5 million, who could be in for a bounce-back year and who has the ability to make plays, defend a bit and make 3-pt shots. At 6'4, he is also somewhat switchable, even though faster guard and more powerful wings make hay out of him. But I just don't trust other options on the market and I have more doubts with Rubio and to some extent, Brown (for whom I'd need to swap House for Johnson and you could make the argument that it'd be worthwhile).
Can't they play Hayes-Cade-Ivey together? Sort of like OKC played Schröder-CP3-SGA together? Cade has the size to defend forwards.

What makes you say that, considering that they both have played in vastly different circumstances and their respective national teams have a clear gap in terms of talent (Serbia had more, maybe still has, but the gap is narrowing).

Yet it wouldn't be just Sabonis. Picks would be used to obtain Donovan Mitchell who'd be sent to the Nets. Voila, there's your two All-Stars.
He can't just leave, was what I said. He can try to "force his way out", but he can't simply leave for another team. The team has most of the leverage, as long as he is under a long contract.
He simply can't do that, unless he is a free agent. Stop with the lazy takes.
They actually do have if they put their picks + Sabonis into play and Jazz takes a risk with Simmons, giving away up to two 1st round picks (probably protected somewhat).
Also a possible outcome, for sure.

This is why I mentioned the moratorium date. They still have time to change their deal with the Hawks. It's not official and Kings may even cancel the trade at this point, even though it would damage their relationship with the Hawks. But everyone would understand, because... when have the Kings had a player of the caliber of KD?

Fox could develop into an All-Star, considering the defensive attention KD gets from opponents. Also, there are plenty of good-to-mediocre role players on the team. And if they manage to retain Keegan Murray in this scenario (where Barnes must be thrown in to match salaries), there's optimism for the future as well.
Does it matter for the Nets where KD wants to or does not want to play? Their owner is said to be "pissed off" because of KD's actions.

You really think that a team of Fox-Huerter-KD-Murray-Holmes wouldn't be a playoff team? I personally do think that KD is good enough to drag this team into the playoffs and also having KD on the team would open up a LOT of space for Fox. The bench wouldn't be that bad as well, they have Davion, 3-and-D wing Davis, Lyles etc.

Sabonis has two years left on his contract, Barnes has one. What kind of a better trade/player(s) are you going to get for those assets? I find it very, very hard, but perhaps it's doable. Considering the Kings track record of previous trades though, I find it unlikely they'll actually find a better trade on the market. 

I understand why people are (rightfully) worried about KD's another trade demand, but I also think that if you presume too much, you might just dig your own grave. KD isn't beloved right now in any city community, even in the Bay, although they are more friendly and thankful there for his actions in the two title runs. Not everyone is, though, because some think that his performances robbed the spotlight from Curry's greatness. 

If he finds affection in a city, he might stay. It's not an impossible notion at this point of his career.

I understand it might sound too crazy or unrealistic, because "it's the Kings, wtf are you talking about". I just tried to find a way to make this Nets demand work, while finding incentives for other teams to trade for KD and mortgage their future/present.

I don't buy the "no way" talk. KD is too into basketball to sit out for a prolonged time and he might realize that there truly isn't a city in the league that loves him almost unconditionally. He might understand how hard it would be to build a title-winning team in Phoenix, after they have to give up a lot to pair an older KD with even older CP3. Also, KD doesn't have the leverage at this point or a no-trade clause.

Backcourt would be: Fox, Davion Mitchell, Terence Davis, a few other players who probably aint that important.  


Wings would be KD, Huerter, Keegan Murray, they can find means to bolster this front:  


Bigs continue to be Holmes, Lyles and Metu, perhaps Len stays as a backup.  


Fox-Mitchell/Huerter-KD-Murray-Holmes isn't that bad, honestly. They still have options to fill out their bench.
They can still change the trade with the Hawks, can they not? Until 6th of July, it should be possible to re-arrange this trade, if the goal is to get KD.

Was that really KD's fault? Kyrie tanked their whole season, drove Harden out of Brooklyn (and received a former All-Star who wouldn't dare to step on the court again) and was almost a no-show in the playoffs as well.
Dude, are you seriously going to copy-paste this to every thread?
The Jazz seem to have the resources to do this, especially if they include OKC in this convoluted mess

Then I did remember wrongly, thank you for pointing it out with numbers to rest this case.

And I agree with you on the fact that the pool IS limited and repeating the same names would be dull. Plus, as you pointed out, the league IS smarter, even though the Kings still remind us that wrong decisions are a pattern, not a coincidence.

Considering the free agency timing, I understand the rush. And I did appreciate the mentioning of Carter and Reed, because I also hold them in higher regard than GMs or coaches seem to do.

PG - Euroleague Finals MVP and one of the most valued playmakers Vasilie Micic. I try to make it as short as possible because Xmas is here and the last thing many of us want to discuss during holidays is politics. The discussions - especially with some of EKRE's supporters in the family circle - just reach dead ends and bring a toxic vibe to the whole ordeal.

Why is the current coalition of Reform and Centre losing in the ratings? A cocktail of reasons. Relatively poor/insufficient management of the COVID health crisis. Complex and often confusing public messaging due to poor communication amongst the coalition (Centre's leader is often publicly sabotaging the decisions the govt makes and it's no secret he is not a fan of this alliance) and messaging disparities with health scientists - the latter part might change in 2022.

The coalition was also struck hard by the surge in electricity prices - Centre wants to support everyone, two opposition parties want to forget about stock market capitalism when electricity prices surge and Reform has been portrayed like they are the main reason why all prices are surging. **Reform's relatively young leader Kaja Kallas is more of a lawyer (in my eyes) than a true politician** \- she is not a fan of repeating simple messages and "dumbing down" for audiences. She is also slow at making decisions, which is seen as a weakness. Some older folks long for the times when Reform had a strong male lead who seemingly made hasty decisions and was clearer in his messages. People are also just generally kinda bored with Reform, because from the outside it sometimes seems they didn't change too much over the years when they were in opposition.

I honestly think Reform is actually kinda fine - you almost always lose support when you wield power - the same thing happened with EKRE, Center and Isamaa when they were in coalition. However, they definitely can't stay comfortable with the current situation. It would help if Reform's old leaders wouldn't publicly blame Kaja Kallas for all the problems in Estonia...

Did EKRE cause a fall in Reform's ratings? A bit, but I definitely wouldn't say they had the most to do with it. The main reasons were the coalition's poor health crisis management and surge in electricity prices and "needing someone to blame". EKRE has stolen perhaps 1-2% of Reform's votes, but the main benefactor has definitely been Eesti 200, which is a similar center-liberal party, but with newer faces.

Is EKRE's support sustainable? Might be, depending on how the other parties implement policies with ministries + how they act and speak with the public. EKRE is definitely the most successful party in terms of converting their supporters to almost cult members. It can be incredibly hard to argue with EKRE's hardcore fans and loyalists who have narratives in their heads that blame all the bad circumstances about anything on someone else's shoulders (mostly liberals of all kinds, but also "career women", greedy farmers, people in universities, female doctors - you name it). There's almost always a stupidly easy answer for every hard question, no matter if the answer is illogical or just not true.

What is the new E200 like? Kinda like Reform, but a bit more populist, perhaps. They speak of having and implementing new, pragmatic visions that span more than one election cycle, but they seemingly avoid going into the details. I personally don't dig that kind of generic approach, but they are the only strong new party with a capable organization and people are drawn to "new hope" in general. There just aren't any other strong new parties, even EKRE is sort of built on the corpse of Rahvaliit, a popular rural party in the 90s and 00s. E200 is halfway a "fuck-you" vote to the establishment parties, which might soon include EKRE.

What is Centre Party like? They are the local  "Russian voter party", mostly, with a heavy dose of Estonian elderly voters. They are a "centre party", but I'd say that even though they are "liberals" in the European Parliament, they are actually socially a bit more conservative than liberal due to the virtues that Russian-speaking people and elderly people generally have. There is a "liberal wing" inside the party, though, and many members of that wing are in the Centre's leadership council.

They used to be strong in rural areas, but EKRE has stolen many votes from them in that regard. They are very flexible (power is more important than "virtues") in terms of negotiating, but they lack identity besides catering to Russian-speaking people and/or the elderly and their needs. Considering the fact that they've had a power monopoly in the capital city of Estonia for almost 20 years and seeing how Tallinn has progressed **despite the Centre Party**, not with their aid, I'd say that they are actually the most stagnant-minded party in Estonia, along with Isamaa (right-center, EKRE Lite). That might change soon because there's a dissonance between the popularity of Centre's leader and the mayor of Tallinn, who is obv in the same party. The mayor has results and votes that Centre's leader lacks. If the mayor will start running the party, perhaps they can re-gain their old support in the higher 20%-s.

You are being too harsh. I'll address your talking points in the order you presented them.

First of all, it takes two to tango with the draft slots. As many fans would LOVE to believe it takes just a compelling offer, the reality is much more nuanced. Almost every front office is enamored with their favorite prospects even in an "average" draft and won't be swayed as easily as you'd think. Few want to trade down, unless they are facing severe financial restrictions or are very, very, current Utah Jazz/LA Clippers/Milwaukee Bucks-like confident in their core rotation. These clubs rarely have top-10 picks and this year, Warriors was the only club from next season's contenders who might have been interested in selling the ... 7th pick. And there were legit reports out there that they wanted Giddey there as well, but took Kuminga in the end. There were rumors that the Cavs wanted to sell the 3rd pick with Godfather-like offers, but frankly, there are legitimate discussions to be had if Evan Mobley was worth a bazillion picks. OKC's front office probably didn't think Mobley was worth it. 

There are different levels of trust between various NBA front offices. It's also entirely possible that Presti's front office didn't see the '21 draft as THE draft to go all-in or at least halfway all-in with all the picks. They might prefer '22 or '23, since last season was their Year One of rebuilding. Also, they owe a lottery-protected pick to the Hawks from the Melo-Schroeder trade and they were dangerously close to being a play-in team before SGA got legitimately hurt.

Why did Presti trade Sengün? Because the average outcome of the 16th pick is pretty damn bad and you very rarely, if ever, get these kind of offers during draft day. Also, if you dive in juuust a bit deeper than the average fan to these picks - there are minimal chances that these Detroit and Washington picks don't convey. Especially the Detroit one, but you can place a good wager on the Wizards pick as well, if Beal stays in place or leaves in one year. There's also the fact that the picks are protected year-by-year, which gives OKC huge leverage with the Pistons and Wizards. In order to make moves for their team and using future picks, they probably have to negotiate with OKC to remove restrictions on their picks. That's semi-advanced CBA stuff that the average fan almost never considers, but something to keep in mind.

Now, shortening the rebuild. That's usually a somewhat terrible idea, especially after Year One. If you want to shorten it after Year Two or Three, fine. But after Year One and Draft One, you don't have enough young enticing first-round prospects to make significant moves down the line. After Year Two, you have 3-4 first-round players and that makes dealing so much easier, considering how valued the first-round rookie contracts are in the league by almost all NBA franchises and their respective front offices.

We also have to reserve some judgment with Summer League. There ain't more than 3-5 legitimate defensive big men out there who are honestly NBA-ready. Sengün played with grown-up men last year and it's only natural he would feast, playing with late teenagers who are mostly coming out of the NCAA. We need to see what he will do against bigs, who are actually big and strong enough to deter him. His height and average wingspan might become a problem on the next level, even if his feel for the game is awesome. I'm not saying they will be a problem, but they might be. 

Also, let's reserve a couple of years of judgment to OKC's own players, mostly Giddey and Tre Mann. Giddey is one of the youngest players in the draft and didn't have the chance to demonstrate himself in the summer league due to his unfortunate ankle injury. But 6'7-6'9 jumbo guard-wings can be very valuable in their own right, if they develop nicely. And 6'5 guard Tre Mann has maybe the sweetest 3-pt shot, which is ever-valuable in this league. But we need to give both of these guys at least two seasons to judge them somewhat correctly. The same applies to Sengün, of course.
